comment: more homes here makes sense. 46 floors twice over is a lot though, still trying to picture it
Fine with the smaller building for shops or whatever ends up there. The towers? no thanks. I didn't move here to live beside two giant filing cabinets.
1170 homes. yes please
I live nearby and I'm undecided. A street-level drawing would be more useful to me than the storey count on its own. Hard to understand how the separate building sits between everything.
46 STOREYS?? Both of them?? Put them somewhere else, this is already a neighbourhood.
work round here, more customers would be welcome tbh. depends what goes in that smaller building but the idea is good
Deliveries are already the thing I have to plan my working day around. I'm worried about construction access, not saying it can't be managed. Just not convinced by what's here so far.
pass through most weekdays. happy to see homes added, no real opinion on the other bit
need a site plan. cant rate a building I cant picture
The smaller building sounds interesting. Only here now and then so not taking a strong position on the whole thing
Yes. This is the scale of housing we need to be considering. I'd like to see the application progress rather than spend years arguing over whether homes should go here at all.
More housing is good, these particular towers aren't for me. Too tall.
Generally in favour. What would the wind be like at ground level? Not assuming it'll be bad, I just want to know before pretending I understand the design.
looks promising :) no idea what the non-residential space is going to be so skipped a confident answer there
restaurant yes, hotel no. six storeys feels like a lot on this street
I'm nearby and I actually like it. A hotel on a commercial street isn't a strange idea to me. Would be good to see how they handle deliveries and arrivals.
Nope. I like visiting hotels when I'M on holiday, doesn't mean I want one beside me!! Housing instead please.
Where do deliveries go / where do taxis stop? genuine question, couldn't tell from this
I work nearby. Visitors staying overnight could be good for shops here, not just the restaurant in the building. I'm for it
The restaurant sounds fine. Hotel activity is what bothers me... late arrivals, bags, cars etc. I don't know how much there would be but I'm not sold.
more people staying local = potentially more business. no strong feelings about the restaurant bit
would stay here! I visit the area anyway
Another place to eat, sure. Can't say much about the hotel itself from a visit once in a while
i commute through, not enough info for a useful opinion sorry
I'd rather see apartments. That's why I'm opposed, not because a restaurant is some terrible thing.
still weighing it up. like the dining part
Restaurant gets a yes from me. Need to understand the hotel operation a bit more before deciding on that half
I like this street how it is. Maybe selfish but that's my answer. Not convinced the hotel improves it
6 storeys behind the medical building seems reasonable to me. glad they're keeping the front building
Keep the medical building, absolutely. Not keen on adding this much at the rear though, would like to see the actual layout
homes + medical building staying. good
I'm nearby but haven't decided. How do you get between the buildings? I need a plan I can actually read, not just the description.
I work in the medical building. Happy it's staying. My main question is how people coming for appointments would get in while construction happens; that needs a proper explanation.
Two uses on one site could get complicated for servicing. Keeping the medical space is good but I don't support the residential part as described
come here for appointments. pleased the medical building stays! housing behind it sounds fine
Medical building stays, thats the important part for me. Can't really judge the rear building yet
on Neilson a lot, more homes seems fine. dont use the medical building so neutral there
I worry about cars going in and out. I haven't seen a traffic study, just giving my concern as someone who travels past.
This is the sort of thing I like seeing: add housing without removing the medical building. Strongly in favour
No more buildings in the back please. I enjoy looking at less building. Yes I know that's not much of a planning argument.
neutral about the housing. keeping the medical building gets my vote
unsure on both, need more than this to go on
replacement homes and new affordable ones are what matter most to me. Market part I'm pretty neutral on
yes to the homes AND the parks. would like this to go ahead
I'm for replacing the social housing and adding affordable homes. Still against the overall plan at this scale. Those aren't contradictory things to me

What happens first? I'm trying to understand what the work would mean for people living here now, and the notice doesn't really get into the sequence. Not assuming an outcome either way. Just need something clearer before I pick support or oppose.
Looks promising overall. Living around a long building project won't be fun but that doesn't automatically make the plan a bad idea
6 to 25 storeys... can we just have ONE thing that doesn't turn into a giant redevelopment? Not in favour. Don't fully understand the replacement part yet either
good on the social / affordable homes. undecided on the package
Affordable homes, replacement homes, parks = yes. Wish the mix wasn't so heavy on market housing though
I work nearby and think more housing plus community space could be good. It's a big proposal, but there are things here worth supporting.
not against affordable homes. I just worry the disruption will go on forever, and that leaves me against this plan overall
like the streets and parks idea. don't know enough about the housing arrangements to rate them all
I visit family here. Replacement homes matter a lot to me; more useful public space would be welcome too.
Replacement social housing AND new affordable homes. Strong yes from me. The market homes can be part of it too
support the affordable bits. not convinced by this overall mix, feels like the wrong balance to me
facility sounds good. no firm opinion on a lease when I haven't seen the terms
Community amenities? interested. A long lease on city land? much less enthusiastic. Those are different decisions in my head
yes please!! basketball facility nearby would be great
What does 'community amenities' actually mean here. Who gets in? when? Not seeing enough to decide
I'd prefer something else on this land. I don't even like basketball. A very large quiet patch of nothing would suit me fine thanks.
work nearby, would welcome it. know we haven't been told the access details yet
Not sold on tying up the land for a long time. Can't really judge the amenities without knowing what they are
pass Fleet regularly. like the recreation idea, no strong view overall
As a basketball fan: YES. pretty excited about this one
The amenities part sounds good, but I don't know whether I'd ever actually be able to use them. Not assuming public hours or anything from that wording.
Seems a worthwhile use of the property. I'm in favour of the facility and the lease as proposed
Could be a useful facility. Still uneasy about a long commitment of public land, so I'm against the proposal overall
need more detail on the amenities. neutral for now
I visit for recreation. Would rather the City keep its options open on the land, even if a practice facility is a perfectly fine idea elsewhere
I go through Six Points all the time and still can't tell where these bits are from the legal description. map please
Support the specified closures overall. Neutral about the Kipling parcel
not comfortable with the Dundas parts. haven't made my mind up on the others
These are bits of road land, not the whole streets. Understood that much! Still can't picture the Bloor piece so unsure on that one
I'm nearby and support the listed closures. Not reading this as shutting down entire streets
Dundas parts seem OK to me. Don't favour the Kipling or Bloor ones
PART OF PIN this, PART OF LOT that... I just want to know which bit of pavement we're talking about lol. undecided
I work round here and worry about access. To be fair, I can't tell whether my concern even applies to these particular parcels. That's why the plan matters
yes for the Dundas and Kipling portions. no strong view on the Bloor piece
only visit occasionally, need the plan not just street names
seems pretty local / parcel specific. don't have a strong view from elsewhere in the city
NO to permanent closures. I might want that bit of road one day. Don't ask me which bit, that's what the map is for!!
Support these particular parcel closures. fine with all three
generally for it, particularly the Kipling and Bloor bits. neutral on Dundas
